methods.label: Find both diagonals
methods.explanation:
The common endpoint of the two chord sides lies on the circle. Joining it to the center therefore gives another radius, which is a diagonal of the rhombus.

Label the rhombus \(OAPB\) in order, where \(O\) is the center, \(OA,OB\) are the radius sides, and \(AP,PB\) are the chord sides. Since \(P\) lies on the circle, \(OP=16\). Every rhombus side also has length sixteen.

Let \(M\) be the intersection of diagonals \(OP\) and \(AB\). A rhombus's diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so \(OM=8\). In right triangle \(OMA\),
\[
AM=\sqrt{16^2-8^2}=\sqrt{192}=8\sqrt3.
\]
Thus \(AB=2AM=16\sqrt3\). The area is half the product of the diagonals:
\[
\frac12\cdot16\cdot16\sqrt3
=\boxed{128\sqrt3\text{ square feet}},
\]
choice B.
